title: $7,500 a year for 30 years. The Roth math.

concepts.title: The inputs: $7,500 × 30 years
concepts.body: The 2026 Roth IRA limit is $7,500. Compound that over thirty years at a 7% real return. Future-value of an annuity formula. The math is unforgiving — and the result is staggering.

concepts.title: The result: ~$708,000
concepts.body: Future value of $7,500 per year for 30 years at 7% real return is roughly $708,000. Of that, you contributed $225,000. The remaining $483,000 is tax-free compound growth. That's the Roth's compounding engine.

concepts.title: The split: $225k in, $483k growth
concepts.body: Your contributions: $225,000 over 30 years. Tax-free growth: roughly $483,000. The growth is more than double your contributions. The Roth is a tax-free compounding engine — that's the whole point.

sources: S&P 500 historical real return — 7% (Damodaran, NYU Stern, 2026 update)
Future-value-of-annuity formula: FV = PMT × [((1 + r)^n - 1) / r]
